name: Life Insurance Corporation of India
title: Life Insurance Corporation of India - 543526 - Transcript Of Earning Conference Call With The Analyst/Investors

summary.headline: LIC Q1 FY27 net VNB margin rose 750 bps YoY to 22.9% and VNB grew 61.32% to ₹3,136 crore; profit after tax up 22.81% to ₹13,492 crore.
summary.overview: LIC reported Q1 FY27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026) with total premium of ₹127,250 crore (+6.75% YoY) and individual new business premium of ₹14,351 crore (+14.48% YoY). Net VNB margin expanded to 22.9% from 15.4%, driven mainly by business mix (non-par savings and protection growth) and a 2.9% positive assumption impact, partly offset by a 1.9% negative expense impact from loss of GST input tax credit. Overall market share by first-year premium fell to 60.10% from 63.51%, with group share down to 70.90% and individual share up to 38.89%. The company also disclosed the 6.5% government OFS, taking public float to 10%.

segments.name: Individual business
segments.commentary: Individual new business premium ₹14,351 crore (+14.48%); individual renewal premium ₹61,065 crore (+3.61%); individual APE ₹7,532 crore with non-par share rising to 32.49% from 30.34%. ULIP premium declined YoY.

segments.name: Group business
segments.commentary: Group total premium ₹51,834 crore (+8.61%); group APE ₹6,160 crore; group market share fell to 70.90% from 76.54% on a comparable basis.

segments.name: Par vs non-par (APE)
segments.commentary: Par individual APE ₹5,085 crore (67.51% of individual APE); non-par ₹2,447 crore (32.49%). Management cited non-par savings growth of 59.24% and non-par protection growth of 43.59%.

segments.name: Bancassurance and alternate channels
segments.commentary: NBP ₹907.14 crore (+5.25%); bank channel NBP ₹483.39 crore (-8.62%) due to delayed bank marketing plans and West Asia related remittance pressure on annuities; alternate channels ₹423.75 crore (+27.27%).

capex_capacity: The call did not discuss capex, capacity, utilisation, or commissioning timelines; no capex plans were stated.

Product pipeline: two new products launched since April 2026 (New Jeevan Sathi single premium and limited premium); Nav Jeevan Shree single premium withdrawn. Total of 59 products available for new business as of 30 June 2026.

Digital and distribution capacity: MyLIC and Super Sales Saathi apps launched in April 2026 under the DIVE initiative; agent-assisted Ananda application completed 436,925 policies in Q1 FY27 (+25.56% YoY).
Bima Sakhi rollout: 2.87 lakh women designated, covering 151,620 of 244,876 gram panchayats (62%) as of 30 June 2026; target is at least one Bima Sakhi per gram panchayat.
Agent force: 1,445,692 agents as of 30 June 2026 (-2.73% YoY); management said non-serious Bima Sakhi recruits are being weeded out, which will continue.
guidance_outlook: Management does not normally give guidance but expects VNB margin to keep improving over the next few quarters, subject to RFR movements.
Management said VNB margin should settle around the industry average and is working toward mid-20s VNB margin by year end.
Non-par growth expected to continue from Q1 to Q4 pattern; ULIP recovery expected when market normalises.
Expense ratio expected to fall with operational efficiency; GST ITC-related expense impact to be compared against last year in Q1 and Q2 only.
Bancassurance expected to recover in subsequent quarters after delayed bank marketing plans.
APE growth expected to strengthen in subsequent quarters as new business focus increases through the year.
demand_pricing: Individual protection growth above 40% YoY on a small base; individual agents drove most protection policy volume.
ULIP premium declined YoY due to market volatility; management said it expects recovery only when markets normalise and denied cannibalisation of non-par.
Average ticket size rose after minimum sum assured for the major regular-premium product was raised from ₹1 lakh to ₹2 lakh (October 2024) and annuity single-premium sales grew.
Agent count fell 2.73% YoY to 1,445,692 (market share by agent count 43.69% vs 47.11%) as non-serious Bima Sakhi recruits quit; agency sold 98.51% of policies and 93.07% of new business premium.
Renewal commission growth declined YoY, attributed to agents no longer in the books and not eligible to renew commission.

qa_highlights.question: What are the assumption changes in the VNB walk and is the cost impact GST-led?
qa_highlights.answer: Assumption changes contributed +2.9% (RFR, persistency alignment, CRNHR, TVOG); expense assumptions including loss of ITC contributed -1.9%. Business mix contributed about +6.5%. The GST exemption removed ITC, adding to expenses, but higher volumes should dilute per-policy expenses.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ULIP decline deliberate and will it recover in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly market-driven due to volatility; management focused on margin-accretive non-par lines. ULIP recovery depends on market improvement; no cannibalisation expected.

qa_highlights.question: Why does RWRP differ from individual APE?
qa_highlights.answer: APE annualises new business premium by frequency and excludes first-year renewal premiums received after policy completion; RWRP captures actual premium received, so the gap reflects strong first-year renewal premium.

qa_highlights.question: Why is APE growth soft despite strong VNB growth, and what is the medium-term aspiration?
qa_highlights.answer: Prior-year base had higher regular-premium share; management expects APE growth to pick up in later quarters. No numeric medium-term target given; management agreed to examine monthly APE disclosure.

qa_highlights.question: Split of VNB margin by line of business?
qa_highlights.answer: Par: 37.1% of APE with 19.4% margin; individual non-par: ₹1,678 crore APE with 49.3% margin; group: 45% of APE with 29.4% margin (figures given as shares of VNB as well as APE by the Appointed Actuary, clarified as proportion of VNB by segment).

qa_highlights.question: Why is the solvency ratio high and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: 2.42 is pre-dividend; 2.32 after subsequent dividend. Higher solvency supports protection growth, but management will await regulatory changes before deciding on any change to solvency strategy.

qa_highlights.question: Why is bancassurance individual NBP growing much slower than policy count?
qa_highlights.answer: Bank channel faced pressure from West Asia conflict affecting remittances (annuities) and market volatility (ULIPs); low-ticket policies were withdrawn after minimum sum assured rose to ₹2 lakh.

qa_highlights.question: Is VNB margin on track for mid-20s by year end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is working toward that target.

risks_watch: Assumption and RFR movements: RFR contributed positively, but management said it is outside LIC's control and could change the margin trajectory.
Persistency weakness: 61-month premium persistency fell to 61.12% from 63.85%; 13-month number-based persistency rose to 66.45% from 64.35%; group persistency contributed negatively to assumptions.
Market share erosion: overall first-year premium share fell to 60.10% from 63.51%; group share fell sharply.
Expense ratio up 16 bps YoY to 10.63% after loss of GST input tax credit; volume growth must outpace expense growth.
Maturity claims up 12.88% YoY to ₹57,099 crore; agent count down 2.73% YoY.
Bancassurance bank channel NBP down 8.62%; recovery timing uncertain.
Solvency pre-dividend 2.42, post-dividend 2.32; any capital needs for protection growth require monitoring.
Shareholder profit from ASM funds (₹180,000 crore book value) and par surplus transfer timing (mainly Q4) affect quarterly profit comparisons.
IEV unwind and EV not disclosed quarterly; next disclosure at half-year.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and profit growth, with explicit caution on ULIP, bancassurance and APE momentum, which management attributed to market volatility and timing. Management was evasive on specific assumption splits and unwind rates, deferring to the half-year EV/IEV disclosure.
key_quotes: We expect the margins to improve.
So APE and WRP cannot be equal.
We would like to see that the non-par growth continues the way it has been growing from Q1 to Q4 over the previous years that will continue in the current year as well.
We don't normally give a guidance, but we expect it to improve over the next few quarters as well, of course, keeping the one uncertain factor of the RFR.

growth.why: Management does not give formal numeric guidance but expects VNB margin to keep improving toward mid-20s by year end and APE growth to strengthen; backing is product launches, mix shift to non-par, Bima Sakhi distribution and expense efficiency, with no capacity additions or capex discussed.
